title: Credit Card Fraud — LDS1071

figures.title: Fraud prevalence and completeness
figures.read: Quantify the rare positive class and inspect missing-value counts before modeling.
figures.interpret: Accuracy alone is inadequate under strong imbalance; use ranking and precision-recall metrics.
figures.limitation: Verify the competition target and input schema; missingness is data quality, not model quality.

figures.title: Numerical feature distributions
figures.read: Compare scales, tails, discreteness and potential heavy skew across numerical variables.
figures.interpret: Long-tailed variables motivate robust plots, transformations or nonlinear modeling.
figures.limitation: Distributional shape does not itself prove fraud discrimination.

figures.title: Distributions conditioned on fraud status
figures.read: Compare selected numerical densities between legitimate and fraudulent transactions.
figures.interpret: Separation indicates candidate signal, while overlap suggests the need for joint models.
figures.limitation: Class-normalized densities conceal the underlying prevalence difference.

figures.title: Pearson versus Spearman correlation
figures.read: Compare linear correlation with rank/monotonic association among features.
figures.interpret: Different matrices indicate relationships that may not be captured by linear correlation alone.
figures.limitation: Correlation is not causation; feature dependence can destabilize interpretation.

figures.title: Fraud prevalence across categories
figures.read: Compare base rates by categorical groups while checking category frequencies.
figures.interpret: High-rate categories may be informative, especially when supported by many observations.
figures.limitation: Tiny groups can show unstable rates; inspect support and confidence intervals.

figures.title: Boolean flags: frequency versus risk
figures.read: Contrast how common each Boolean flag is with its conditional fraud rate.
figures.interpret: A rare flag can be highly discriminative; prevalence and risk answer different questions.
figures.limitation: A high marginal fraud rate need not persist after adjusting for other variables.

figures.title: Quantile-binned fraud-rate curves
figures.read: Estimate observed fraud probabilities across ordered feature bins.
figures.interpret: Curved or nonmonotone rates motivate splines and boosted trees beyond a linear logit.
figures.limitation: Binning and sparse tails introduce uncertainty; curves are descriptive.

figures.title: Transaction timing and fraud
figures.read: Compare fraud rates by hour and day, with uncertainty information where available.
figures.interpret: Temporal changes can improve features or motivate periodic transformations.
figures.limitation: These are aggregated clock patterns, not temporal leakage tests.

figures.title: Joint numerical risk surfaces
figures.read: Study the joint variation in fraud rates for pairs of numeric predictors.
figures.interpret: A strong high-high cell can signal interactions that additive linear models miss.
figures.limitation: Cells with low support can exaggerate apparent contrasts.

figures.title: Univariate outlier fences
figures.read: Count extreme observations using robust, IQR-based thresholds.
figures.interpret: Unusual values deserve inspection but are not automatically recording errors.
figures.limitation: Unsupervised fences do not identify fraud labels or causality.

figures.title: Isolation Forest anomaly scores
figures.read: Compare anomaly scores with empirical fraud prevalence on the diagnostic sample.
figures.interpret: Anomaly enrichment can reveal useful risk prioritization signals.
figures.limitation: In-sample associations do not establish independent fraud-detection performance.

figures.title: Candidate ROC AUC and fold variation
figures.read: Rank modeling specifications by pooled out-of-fold ROC AUC and inspect fold variability.
figures.interpret: Read pooled score together with the spread across five validation folds.
figures.limitation: Selection and reported performance on the same OOF predictions can be optimistic.

figures.title: Correlation among model predictions
figures.read: Measure redundancy among candidate probability scores.
figures.interpret: Highly correlated models contribute less diversity to naive probability averaging.
figures.limitation: High correlation does not imply identical ranking of the top-risk transactions.

figures.title: Single models versus probability blends
figures.read: Compare best single model, top-k blend, family representatives and all-candidate blend.
figures.interpret: More members do not guarantee higher ROC AUC or average precision.
figures.limitation: Blend membership selected on OOF results requires fresh evaluation for unbiased claims.

figures.title: ROC and precision–recall curves
figures.read: Inspect discrimination over many thresholds instead of one arbitrary cutoff.
figures.interpret: ROC AUC measures ranking; precision–recall is highly sensitive to fraud rarity.
figures.limitation: Threshold-free metrics do not choose a deployment threshold.

figures.title: How many principal components explain 90%?
figures.read: Use singular values/eigenvalues to inspect retained feature variance.
figures.interpret: High explained input variance does not necessarily preserve rare-class discrimination.
figures.limitation: Fit PCA only inside CV training folds to avoid leakage.

figures.title: Logistic assumptions and feature shift
figures.read: Inspect multicollinearity diagnostics and exploratory feature-shift measures.
figures.interpret: Reference-category encoding limits exact dummy redundancy; regularization improves stability.
figures.limitation: A low VIF does not verify independence or correct logit specification.

figures.title: OOF logistic diagnostics
figures.read: Compare logistic residual behavior, calibration and convergence information.
figures.interpret: A nonlinear residual pattern motivates a more flexible conditional probability model.
figures.limitation: Descriptive out-of-fold checks do not verify all statistical assumptions.

figures.title: Gradient boosting as a logit correction
figures.read: Compare baseline logistic results with XGBoost that adds nonlinear log-odds corrections.
figures.interpret: The boosted stage models corrections rather than replacing the linear baseline.
figures.limitation: Only held-out metrics can establish whether the added flexibility helps.

figures.title: Predictive ability of individual features
figures.read: Rank single predictors by univariate discrimination and direction of association.
figures.interpret: Strong individual signals help explain candidate selection and model interpretation.
figures.limitation: Univariate AUC ignores interactions and redundant information.

figures.title: Empirical CDFs by outcome
figures.read: Compare cumulative numerical distributions for legitimate and fraud cases.
figures.interpret: Widening ECDF gaps highlight thresholds or ranges with class separation.
figures.limitation: Do not interpret class-normalized curves as population fraud probabilities.

figures.title: Categorical × Boolean interactions
figures.read: Compare conditional fraud rates and support across joint feature groups.
figures.interpret: Interactions can expose differences hidden in one-feature plots.
figures.limitation: Sparse combinations should be interpreted with support counts in view.

figures.title: Hour-of-week risk heatmaps
figures.read: Visualize fraud rate and observation counts jointly across time coordinates.
figures.interpret: Rate patterns are more credible where sample support is substantial.
figures.limitation: No causal or temporal stability guarantee follows from one observed period.

figures.title: Fraud geometry in two dimensions
figures.read: Inspect selected feature pairs for overlap, clusters and unusual regions.
figures.interpret: Nonlinear class boundaries may explain why trees compete with additive models.
figures.limitation: Plotting subsamples can distort apparent density and class composition.

figures.title: Train–test distribution comparisons
figures.read: Compare unlabeled feature distributions between training and test splits.
figures.interpret: A visible shift warns that held-out CV may not exactly match test conditions.
figures.limitation: Without test labels, score deterioration cannot be quantified directly.

figures.title: A four-metric model scorecard
figures.read: Compare ROC AUC, average precision, log loss and Brier loss.
figures.interpret: Ranking quality and probability quality need not order models identically.
figures.limitation: Choose a primary metric before interpreting many scores.

figures.title: Predictive quality versus compute cost
figures.read: Plot candidate performance against wall-clock training expense.
figures.interpret: Small gains may not justify large computation on a teaching project.
figures.limitation: Times depend on hardware, device, threading and cache state.

figures.title: Predicted-risk distributions by class
figures.read: Compare predicted fraud probabilities for legitimate and fraud cases.
figures.interpret: Overlap reveals unavoidable false positives and false negatives at any cutoff.
figures.limitation: These are out-of-fold scores, not deployment calibration guarantees.

figures.title: Cumulative gains and lift
figures.read: Measure how many fraud cases are captured within the highest-ranked transactions.
figures.interpret: Lift compares model-guided review against random screening at the same budget.
figures.limitation: Operational usefulness depends on review costs and achievable capacity.

figures.title: Precision and recall at limited review budget
figures.read: Examine quality as the fraction of investigated transactions increases.
figures.interpret: Fraud screening is a ranking-and-capacity problem, not only 0.5 classification.
figures.limitation: Selecting capacity using the same OOF labels can induce optimism.

figures.title: Confusion matrices under two decision rules
figures.read: Contrast fixed 0.5 probability threshold with an intervention budget (top 1%).
figures.interpret: Threshold selection materially changes precision, recall and false alarms.
figures.limitation: Never transfer a threshold across populations without validation.

figures.title: Reliability diagrams across models
figures.read: Compare observed fraud frequency against predicted risk by score bin.
figures.interpret: A model may rank well but still misstate absolute risk.
figures.limitation: Rare-event bins require caution, especially near extreme predicted risks.

figures.title: Calibration uncertainty intervals
figures.read: Plot uncertainty around observed bin-level fraud rates.
figures.interpret: Wide intervals reveal where limited positive counts weaken conclusions.
figures.limitation: Intervals summarize within-bin sampling variation, not all sources of model uncertainty.

figures.title: Model quality across channels
figures.read: Compare discrimination by transaction channel for selected candidates.
figures.interpret: Subgroup metrics can reveal heterogeneous predictive behavior.
figures.limitation: Subgroup sample sizes and fraud counts determine precision.

figures.title: Model quality across merchant categories
figures.read: Examine predictive quality across major merchant groups.
figures.interpret: A strong global score can conceal weaker performance in some subgroups.
figures.limitation: Small subgroup differences may be sampling noise; avoid overinterpretation.

figures.title: Agreement among the top 1% riskiest cases
figures.read: Use Jaccard overlap to compare models on transactions that actually trigger review.
figures.interpret: Highly correlated overall predictions may still disagree at the operational margin.
figures.limitation: The most useful diversity depends on labeling costs and error consequences.

figures.title: Logistic coefficients and tree importances
figures.read: Contrast coefficient-based linear interpretation with tree feature importance.
figures.interpret: Importance notions are model-specific and not on a common causal scale.
figures.limitation: Correlated features and encoding influence apparent importance.

figures.title: Partial dependence: learned nonlinear response
figures.read: Compare average predicted response while varying selected features.
figures.interpret: Different shapes help explain disagreements between linear, spline and tree models.
figures.limitation: Marginal interventions can evaluate unrealistic correlated-feature combinations.

figures.title: How blending changes individual scores
figures.read: Compare selected ensemble predictions against the leading single model.
figures.interpret: Blending can alter risk ordering even when overall metrics barely change.
figures.limitation: A change in predicted probability is not evidence of better calibration.

figures.title: Unlabeled Kaggle submission diagnostics
figures.read: Inspect distribution, extremes and rank behavior of final test probabilities.
figures.interpret: Sanity checks can catch invalid ranges or suspicious collapse of risk scores.
figures.limitation: Unlabeled test plots cannot estimate true predictive accuracy.

figures.title: Effects of model hyperparameters
figures.read: Compare model families, regularization and capacity settings.
figures.interpret: Tree depth, leaf size and learning rate trade expressivity against variance.
figures.limitation: These are tested configurations, not a continuous optimization landscape.

figures.title: Fold-by-fold ROC AUC stability
figures.read: Compare candidate scores across common validation folds.
figures.interpret: Consistent differences are more persuasive than single pooled-rank changes.
figures.limitation: Five folds do not fully quantify sampling uncertainty.

figures.title: Inner grid search: every tested configuration
figures.read: Visualize scikit-learn GridSearchCV scores across the XGBoost/CatBoost candidate grid.
figures.interpret: Grid-search performance selects configurations inside the training data only.
figures.limitation: Best inner-CV score is not the unbiased estimate of final test performance.

figures.title: Did tuning help on held-out outer folds?
figures.read: Compare fixed and tuned families on untouched outer folds, including search cost.
figures.interpret: Use outer-fold results, not the best inner score, to judge tuning benefits.
figures.limitation: Compute-time comparisons are device-dependent; finite-fold differences remain uncertain.

notes: Image-only source. Treat generated charts as supplied; do not infer numerical results or execution provenance not encoded in images.
